newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher, but volumes light.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher, but volumes light.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended higher Monday, on light volumes, with activity dampened by the U.K. bank holiday and the Golden Week holidays in Tokyo.

"In gold there was some fund shortcovering early and some bullion bank buying in a quiet market near the close, but, after finding support around $340 last week, June gold really needs to get above $345.20 to break out of the recent downtrend," North American Equity Services trader, John Geraghty, said.
COMEX June gold ended up $2.70 an ounce at $344.30, after seeing a five day high at $344.80 early.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $342.50/00, compared with the New York close Friday around $339.95/45.

Some analysts argued gold prices firmed on news that Bre-X Mineral Services Ltd's Busang deposit in Indonesia deposit turned out to be fraudulent, meaning an estimated 71 million ounces of mine supply would not now come to market.

Canadian consultants, Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd, released its long-awaited report on the Busang deposit Monday and said the assay results were falsified on a scale "without precedent in the history of mining".

While junior Canadian mining stocks were hit further by the Bre-X news Monday, the broader gold and silver mining sector continued to recover, helped by the firmer gold price and the recovery in the broad U.S. stock market.
The Philadelphia Stock Exchange's gold and silver stock index (.XAU) was up 2.02 percent near the close at 98.60, a 10-day high.
In other news, gold imports into Dubai more than doubled to 155 tonnes in the first quarter this year on the back of strong Indian demand and weak world prices, according to the World Gold Council.

About 85 percent of the 154.90 tonnes imported into Dubai in the first quarter were re-exported to India, where several good monsoon seasons have lifted disposable income and the Indian government has raised the amount non-resident Indians returning to India may import.

"Technically short and intermediate term trends are still down (for gold), but gold prices have traded in a narrow range after the $12 decline between April 11 and April 16," Smith Barney analyst Carmen Knoepffler said.
"This consolidation has resulted in a decline in option implied volatility with premiums currently low from a historical perspective," she said.
"Implied volatility for gold options is down to nine percent for August near-the-money options, near the median of the past three years, but off its recent high over 15 percent."
"The current low volatility level and the potential for increasing volatility favors strategies that involve buying options," she said.
COMEX July silver ended up 4.0 cents at $4.768 an ounce, after seeing a $4.720-4.790 range.

Silver prices have continued to recover from the two year low seen in late April, with the help of fabricator demand, but funds remain net short, analysts said, and may have increased their positions Friday when COMEX silver open interest rose 2,256 lots to 85,219 contracts.
NYMEX July platinum ended up $2.00 at $373.10, while NYMEX June palladium gained $1.00 to $157.90.

"The price trend for palladium remains up as a new 23-month high for the nearby futures was set at $161.45 in late April and there is still no indication of when 1997 PGM export contract talks between Russia and Japan will commence since the decree which would allow negotiations to be begin has yet to be signed," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.
